newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Tunisian insurance market growth slows down.
newsitem.headline: Tunisian insurance market growth slows down.

text.p: The Tunisian insurance market saw growth of 5.52 percent in premiums to 297.45 million dinars in 1995 from 281.88 million dinars in 1994, industry figures showed.
Premiums grew 7.82 percent in 1994 compared to a year earlier.
The Tunisian Federation of Insurance Societies (FTUSA) said the figures excluded exports insurer COFACE and reinsurance firm Tunis-Re.
It said that reimbursed damages amounted to 185.05 million dinars in 1995, up by 13.9 percent compared to 162.47 million dinars in 1994.
Management expenditures were 60.60 million dinars, up by 8.48 percent compared to 55.86 million dinars a year earlier.
Reinsurance technical net result was a loss of 10.22 million dinars in 1995, down by 2.51 percent compared to 10.48 million dinars loss in 1994.
Tunisia has 15 insurance companies. Nine of them are privately-owned and hold nearly 44 percent of market share, two are controlled by the state and four are mutual societies.
The Tunisian government last week told the country's insurance industry it must prepare for an opening up of the market to foreign firms by 1999. ($=0.98 dinar)
